text:
conor: hey y'all, first-day setup snag. running docker-compose up for dev but psql client fails to connect.
conor: docker logs show: "FATAL: could not open lock file '/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432': Permission denied"
conor: compose snippet:
```
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: password
    volumes:
      - ./tmp/postgres:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```
conor: using Mac M1, Docker Desktop 4.x
elaine: ^^ likely a bind-mount ownership issue. macOS + gRPC-FUSE sometimes changes uid/gid. try using a named volume instead of ./tmp/postgres. add `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and top-level `volumes: { pgdata: {} }`
rohan: if you need host dir, chown the host folder to 999:999 (postgres uid/gid in image) `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./tmp/postgres` then restart compose. also check PGDATA env var; some images use /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata
conor: trying chown now...
conor: ok that fixed postgres start 🎉 client can connect via psql now
conor: another odd one — redis in compose uses `command: redis-server --unixsocket /tmp/redis.sock --unixsocketperm 700` but when my app tries to connect it says "Permission denied"
lina: redis socket perms are created inside container and belong to redis user. If your app runs as host user mounting a host dir for /tmp it can mismatch. avoid binding host tmp dir; use TCP (127.0.0.1:6379) for local dev or use named volume
elaine: for socket approach you can set `unixsocketperm 770` and add `unixsocketgroup staff` and add your app to that group — messy. tcp is easier.
conor: switching to TCP and it's all green. thanks!
devops-bot: FYI internal doc on local volumes: https://redwood.internal/dev-setup/postgres-volumes
rohan: tagging @infra for follow-up on adding note to new-hire checklist :thumbsup:
conor: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick help — excited to be here :)
